typed_core.name: issuer_name
typed_core.why: identity — source/preparer org; third-party independence check (processor)

typed_core.name: statement_type
typed_core.why: identity — personal vs business financial statement

typed_core.name: statement_as_of_date
typed_core.why: identity — the point-in-time the balances are stated; recency (processor)

typed_core.name: subject_name
typed_core.why: identity — whose statement (flattened from person_or_entity[]); borrower match

typed_core.name: subject_count
typed_core.why: disambiguator — number of subjects; flags a bad name split

typed_core.name: subject_names_raw
typed_core.why: disambiguator — verbatim name string so a wrong split stays visible

typed_core.name: accounting_basis
typed_core.why: disambiguator — cash vs accrual changes how totals read

typed_core.name: total_assets
typed_core.why: headline — asset base for reserves/net worth

typed_core.name: total_liabilities
typed_core.prompt_hint: Contingent liabilities (guarantees, co-signed notes) are off-balance-sheet — do not fold them into total_liabilities

typed_core.name: net_worth
typed_core.prompt_hint: 'Net worth' = total assets - total liabilities; extract the stated value; a mismatch with the totals is a tag/rule judgment, not something to reconcile at extraction

nested_lists.name: asset_line_items
nested_lists.shape_reason: a personal financial statement lists 10-40 holdings; flat rows keep it well under the 16,384-token ceiling and per-field wrapping would be wasteful for descriptive rows (category, description, value)

fields.name: category
fields.why: asset category (e.g. cash, securities, real estate)

fields.name: description
fields.pii_note: may embed account numbers in free text — treat as potentially sensitive; no _PII_FIELDS path

fields.name: source
fields.why: provenance snippet for the asset row
fields.pii_note: snippet may embed account numbers — treat as potentially sensitive

rejected.name: document_title, form_number, form_revision_date
rejected.reason: classification/version metadata; catch-all suffices, no consumer

rejected.name: issuer_address, issuer_phone, issuer_email_or_url
rejected.reason: contact detail; no rule/processor need for a financial statement

rejected.name: party_addresses, property_address
rejected.reason: not load-bearing on a net-worth statement; no property link needed

rejected.name: loan_number, account_case_reference_number
rejected.reason: linkage nice-to-have; no consumer; catch-all captures

rejected.name: signature_blocks, notary_block, preparer_or_subject_signatures
rejected.reason: a financial statement's execution is not rule-checked; certification_of_accuracy covers attestation

rejected.name: contingent_liabilities, annual_income_by_source
rejected.reason: second/third nested lists; over budget — leave to catch-all unless a rule appears

encoding_variations: statement_type — 'Personal Financial Statement', 'SBA Form 413', 'Statement of Financial Condition'; needs the form/label context to distinguish personal from business
accounting_basis — 'cash basis' vs 'accrual' vs unstated; carry prepared_by alongside so an unlabeled basis can be judged
net_worth — sometimes stated, sometimes only derivable from totals; capture the stated figure verbatim, do not compute

open_questions.q: Which one nested list? asset_line_items vs liability_line_items — both are catalog CORE object[].
options: (c) nest both (2x plumbing, over the one-list budget)
open_questions.recommendation: (a) — assets drive reserve/liquidity use; revisit if an undisclosed-debt rule lands that must read individual liabilities GEET'S DECISION (LP-438): BUILD IT — LP-437 made nested lists cheap (one declaration + the generic mechanism); the one-list-budget / defer / no-consumer concern is overturned. Build as flat_row; the per-rule consumer is separate follow-up.

open_questions.q: subject_names cardinality — flattened to two + count + raw. If a future rule must address a specific business entity vs individual subject separately, revisit.
open_questions.recommendation: keep flat; revisit as person_or_entity[] only if a rule needs subjects addressed individually

open_questions.q: annual_income_by_source — genuinely repeating but no consumer today.
open_questions.recommendation: leaving to catch-all rather than a second nested list

notes: No rules consume this type today, so there is no rule floor; every field earns its place on identity, PII, processor use, or disambiguation.

No restricted PII is typed here. account_case_reference_number is confidential but a document reference, not a person identifier; subject names are standard-sensitivity; no field crosses into _PII_FIELDS.
Asset/liability line items may embed account numbers in free text — the nested source.snippet and description should be treated as potentially sensitive, handled by a row redactor, not _PII_FIELDS.
Prompt hint (doc-level): SBA Form 413 is the most common standardized personal financial statement — capture form_number into the catch-all but read totals from the summary block, not the schedules.
total_assets, total_liabilities, and net_worth are tagged 'headline' in the markdown, which is not one of the five reason_class values; mapped to processor and flagged as ambiguities.
